chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Ja'far from his father, peace be upon them both,
that he used to shorten the prayer when he departed from Kufa at the time of the first prayer he attended.
ai.seo_question: When does a traveler begin shortening their prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the precise moment the ruling of Qasr (shortening prayer) takes effect, establishing that it begins immediately upon exiting the city limits rather than after a specific distance is covered. This specific reference to Kufa highlights the practical application of this rule in the major Shia scholarly centers, reinforcing the view that the city boundary (Hudud al-Madinah) is the trigger for travel status. It serves as a foundational precedent for the jurisprudential consensus that the traveler's status is determined by physical departure from the urban area.
